hypothesis.title: ad service adFailure flag enabled, injecting UNAVAILABLE errors into frontend
hypothesis.summary: The adFailure feature flag in configmap/flagd-config was changed from 'off' to 'on' 10 minutes before the alert. This caused the ad service to inject UNAVAILABLE errors (12.5% error rate), which propagate to frontend as 5xx responses (4.6% error rate). 89% of failing frontend traces terminate in ad with "ad service failure (flag adFailure)". Ad's own resource metrics (CPU, memory, latency) remain healthy, confirming the flag is the direct cause.
hypothesis.reasoning: The alert fired on frontend 5xx errors at 02:50. Tracing the errors upstream: 89% of failing frontend traces end in the ad service with "UNAVAILABLE: ad service failure (flag adFailure)". The ad service itself shows a sharp error rate spike from 0.4% to 12.5% starting around -10m, with 1,296 error logs citing the same flag-driven failure. The critical timing evidence is the config change: configmap/flagd-config changed adFailure from 'off' to 'on' 10 minutes before the alert, which aligns perfectly with when ad errors and frontend errors both began. Ad's own CPU, memory, and latency metrics remain healthy (CPU ~23%, memory ~58%, p95 latency ~29ms), ruling out resource saturation or performance degradation. The recommendation 2.0.2→2.0.3 deploy at -9m and product-catalog 2.0.2→2.0.3 deploy at -14m are red herrings: recommendation is not on the failing trace paths (only 1 of 9 failing traces touched currency, none touched recommendation), and product-catalog's own metrics show no anomalies. The runbook RB-flagd confirms that adFailure is a known failure-injection flag. This is a config_change in the ad service that deliberately injects UNAVAILABLE errors, propagating upstream to frontend.

supporting_evidence.why_it_matters: ConfigMap flagd-config changed adFailure from 'off' to 'on' exactly 10 minutes before the alert, matching the timing of the error spike in ad and frontend.
1,296 ERROR logs in ad explicitly cite 'ad service failure (flag adFailure)', confirming the flag is actively injecting failures.
Failing trace shows the error originates in ad (UNAVAILABLE: ad service failure flag adFailure) and propagates to frontend, establishing the causal chain.
Ad error rate jumped from 0.4% to 12.5% at -10m, coinciding with the config change and proving ad is the source of errors, not a victim.
89% (8 of 9) of failing frontend traces end in ad, confirming ad is the dominant error origin and not a symptom of another service.
1,101 frontend errors calling ad with the same flag-driven message show the error propagation from ad to frontend at scale.

suggested_actions.title: Revert the adFailure flag to 'off' in flagd-config
suggested_actions.command: kubectl -n otel-demo get cm flagd-config -o yaml | sed 's/"adFailure": "on"/"adFailure": "off"/' | kubectl apply -f -
suggested_actions.rationale: The adFailure flag is directly injecting UNAVAILABLE errors. Reverting it to 'off' will immediately stop the error injection. This is the safest and fastest mitigation.

suggested_actions.title: Verify flagd-config rollout and monitor ad error rate
suggested_actions.command: kubectl -n otel-demo get cm flagd-config -o jsonpath='{.data.demo\.flagd\.json}' | jq '.flags.adFailure' && kubectl -n otel-demo logs -l app=ad --tail=50 | grep -i error
suggested_actions.rationale: Confirm the flag has been reverted and check that ad error logs stop appearing. Monitor ad error rate metric to confirm it returns to baseline (~0.4%).

alternatives.why_less_likely: Recommendation deployed 2.0.2→2.0.3 at -9m, but only 1 of 9 failing frontend traces touched currency (not recommendation), and recommendation is not on the call path for the 89% of traces failing in ad. No evidence of errors or anomalies in recommendation's own telemetry.

Product-catalog deployed 2.0.2→2.0.3 at -14m, but there are no error logs, metric spikes, or failing traces involving product-catalog. The timing also predates the error spike by 4 minutes, and product-catalog is not on the failing trace paths.
